messages:
mike-sales: Heads-up — Vendor Risk team at BeaconCo asked for BCP/DR artifacts mapped to SIG/CAIQ items. They need RTO/RPO statements, backup retention & encryption, and a short failover play. Can we draft a slim packet (one pager + attachments)?

customer-rep: They want worst-case numbers and any contractual guarantees. Also asking whether backups are immutable and how restores are audited.

eve-se: Short answers we can include: Hosted API uses cross-region load balancing + active/passive routing. For stateless inference we expect service continuity within ~10–20m after detection. For persisted metadata RPO is typically up to 60m.

toni-security: Add: backups are encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys, stored in WORM-compatible buckets; restore operations require 2-person approval + audit log entry. We'll attach the restore audit sample.

jess-csm: I have a one-page summary template I used for another customer. I'll paste the text and attach the drill summary from Mar 2026.

jess-csm: paste:
"Redwood BCP/DR summary (Hosted) — key points:
- RTO (service continuity): 10–20 minutes for stateless serving via automated failover policies.
- RPO (customer metadata): typical async replication lag < 60 minutes; critical datasets can be configured for tighter RPOs on Dedicated.
- Backups: nightly snapshots + hourly incrementals; default retention 30 days; longer retention via add-on.
- Controls: CMK per-tenant, encrypted at rest, immutable retention options, periodic restore drills.
- SLA: Hosted API contractual availability 99.95% with incident reporting and credit policy."

eve-se: For the SIG mapping, I'll map those bullets to the relevant CAIQ controls (e.g., DR-01 -> RTO statement, DR-02 -> backup policy, DR-03 -> restore test evidence). Want me to create a table?

mike-sales: Keep it prose — legal prefers bullets that map to their checklist. No big tables.

toni-security: Also include a redacted runbook excerpt showing the failover steps (no internal IPs, no run commands). Example snippet below is ok to share:
"Runbook excerpt - automated failover:
1) Monitor triggers: region healthchecks, error rate spike > threshold.
2) Initiate routing change via control plane to secondary region.
3) Promote standby caches and verify model weights are warmed.
4) Confirm KV store replication consistency; if inconsistent, switch to read-only + replay backlog.
5) Validate traffic and metrics; finalize failover and notify stakeholders."

ops-bot: DR drill artifact uploaded: https://redwood.infra/dr/2026-mar/drill-log-03-2026 (access: sales,security,legal).

customer-rep: BeaconCo asked whether we have observed real failovers and what the measured windows were. Can we give a concrete example?

jess-csm: Yes — March tabletop + drill showed an automated failover where detection->traffic shift completed in 14 minutes, full verification and cleanup in 35 minutes. I'll attach the screenshot of the monitoring timeline.

eve-se: For clarity, we should state variability: cold model cache warmups can add extra minutes (we pre-warm common models in standby region to reduce this). Also call out that Dedicated customers can get tighter guarantees with reserved capacity and sync replication.

toni-security: On backups/immutability: we use object-lock for backup buckets with governance mode; restores are tracked with audit IDs. We'll include a sample audit log entry (redacted).

mike-sales: Great. I'll assemble: 1) 1-page summary, 2) redacted runbook excerpt, 3) drill timeline screenshot, 4) backup policy snippet, 5) sample audit log entry, and 6) mapping bullet list to CAIQ items. Send today?

customer-rep: Please send. They may ask follow-ups about encryption key ownership and whether we offer dedicated CMKs.

toni-security: Confirmed: we support customer-managed CMKs for Dedicated and Hosted (via bring-your-key add-on). Note this in the packet.

jess-csm: Packet ready. Uploading now.

mike-sales: Sent to BeaconCo vendor team. Tagging this thread closed unless they request extra tests. Thanks team :rocket:
